<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|18|THE GOSPEL|CHA. VII.}}</noinclude>that knocketh, it shal be opened. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=9}}† Or what man is there of you, vvhom if his childe shal aske bread, vvil he reach him a stone? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=10}}† Or if he shal aske him fish, vvil he reach him a serpent? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=11}}† If you then being naught, knovv hovv to giue good giftes to your children: hovv much more vvil your father vvhich is in heauen, giue {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ These good things are grace and al spiritual gifts, and whatsoeuer pertayneth to the health of the soule.}}∷ good things to them that aske him?

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=12}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 6, 31.''}}* Al things therfore vvhatsoeuer you vvil that men doe to you doe you also to them. For this is the Lavv and the Prophets.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=13}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 13, 24.''}}* Enter ye by the narrovv gate: because brode is the gate, and large is the vvay that leadeth to perdition, and many there be that enter by it. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=14}}† Hovv narrovv is the gate, and straite is the vvay that leadeth to life: and fevv there are that finde it!

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=15}}† {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel on the 7 Sunday after Pentecost.}}Take ye great heede of false Prophets, vvhich come to you in the {{sup|‖}} clothing of sheepe, but invvardly are rauening vvolues. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=16}}† By their {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 6, 44.''}}* {{sup|‖}} fruites you shal knovv them. Do men gather grapes of thornes, or figges of thistels? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=17}}† Euen so euery good tree yeldeth good fruites, and the euil tree yeldeth euil fruites. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=18}}† A good tree can not yeld euil fruites, neither an euil tree yeld good fruites. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=19}}† Euery tree that yeldeth not good fruite, shal be cut dovvne, and shal be cast into fyre. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=20}}† Therfore by their fruites you shal knovv them.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=21}}† Not euery one that sayth to me, {{sup|‖}} Lord, Lord, shal enter into the Kingdom of heauen: but he that doeth the vvil of my father vvhich is in heauen, he shal enter into the kingdom of heauen.⊣ {{verse|chapter=7|verse=22}}† Many shal say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, haue not vve prophecied in thy name, and in thy name cast out diuels, and in thy name vvrought many miracles? {{verse|chapter=7|verse=23}}† And then I vvil cōfesse vnto them, That I neuer knevv you. depart from me you that vvorke iniquitie. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=24}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Luc. 6, 47.''}}* Euery one therfore that heareth these my vvordes, and doeth them: shal be likened to a vvise man that built his house vpon a rocke, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=25}}† and the rayne fel, and the fluddes came, & the vvindes blevve, and they beate agaynst that house, and it fel not, for it vvas founded vpon a rocke. {{verse|chapter=7|verse=26}}† And euery one that heareth these my vvordes, & doeth them not, shal be like a foolish man that built his house vpon the sand, {{verse|chapter=7|verse=27}}† and the rayne fel, and the fluddes came, and the vvindes blevve, and they beate agaynst that house, and it fel, & the fall therof vvas great.

{{verse|chapter=7|verse=28}}† And it came to passe, vvhen {{sc|Iesvs}} had fully ended these vvordes, the multitude vvere in {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 1, 22. Luc. 4, 32.''}}* admiration vpon his<noinclude>{{rh|||doctrine.}}</noinclude>
